### Observed differences

- Outgoing routing of activity A17 is nearly identical across the two windows. In the earlier window, all 58 observed outgoing transitions of A17 went to A40; in the later window, about 97 in 100 of the 38 observed outgoing transitions still went to A40, and a single transition (about 3 in 100) went to A46, which was not observed as a successor of A17 earlier [DIR001].
- The size of this routing difference is very small on the indicator's own scale (cosine dissimilarity of about 0.0004), although it is larger than the differences seen in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits of the pooled traces [DIR001].
- No other behavioural difference qualified at the configured thresholds [DIR001].

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a structural change in the process. Only one indicator qualified, which is of the same order as the roughly 0.46 items expected by chance among the 92 tested units in an unchanged process, and the sole signal — one A17→A46 transition out of 38 observed outgoing transitions in the later window — is precisely the kind of rare variant that sampling differences in variant frequencies produce without any structural change [DIR001].

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

The evidence contains one item: DIR001, a control-flow direction indicator for activity A17. It shows the outgoing transitions of A17:

- Before: A17 → A40 with share 1.0 (100% of observed outgoing transitions)
- After: A17 → A40 with share ~0.974 (about 97 in 100), A17 → A46 with share ~0.026 (about 3 in 100)

Support: 58 outgoing transitions observed before, 38 after. So the after window has only 38 observed outgoing transitions of A17. The new edge A46 appears in about 1 of 38 transitions (0.0263 × 38 ≈ 1). Actually 1/38 = 0.0263. So exactly one occurrence of A17 → A46 in the after window.

Observed change on cosine dissimilarity scale: 0.000365 — tiny. Empirical strength: 0.995, meaning 99.5% of reference comparisons had a smaller difference. But the observed change itself is minuscule on its own scale.

Screening: 92 units tested, 0.46 items expected without change. We have 1 item. Per instructions: "A count of the same order as that expectation (for example one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces: choose 'Insufficient evidence', however large or unusual a single item looks."

1 item vs 0.46 expected — same order. So the verdict must be "Insufficient evidence".

Also, the single occurrence of A17 → A46 in the after window (1 out of 38 outgoing transitions) is exactly the kind of rare variant that can appear in one window only. The support is small (38 transitions after), so a proportion based on 1 observation is weak.

Also note: DIR shares are over observed outgoing transitions, not cases. An unobserved edge before doesn't mean it's absent.
